subtitle: How a Chalukya general raised a stone ‘emperor’ to outlast kings

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of temple front
panels.action: Mahadeva the Commander stands in armor before the towering stone temple of Itagi, sixty-four pillars receding behind him into shadow and light, as the ancient Deccan plain stretches to a hazy horizon.

dialogue.text: In Vikramaditya VI’s war-torn age, one commander—Mahadeva of Itagi—raised a temple so refined that its own stone inscription dared to call it the ‘emperor among temples’.

i18n.hi: विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ के युद्धभरे दौर में ईटगी के सेनापति महादेव ने ऐसा मंदिर उठाया कि उसकी शिलालेख ने उसे खुद ही ‘मंदिरों का सम्राट’ कहकर चुनौती दे दी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on inscription panel carved in stone
panels.action: Close view of a chiselled Kannada inscription on a weathered stone slab near the temple entrance; Mahadeva the Commander’s hand hovers over the letters, his face half in shadow, reading with quiet intensity.

dialogue.text: On a stone at Itagi, scribes cut a proud claim: in the reign of Vikramaditya VI, Mahadeva, a commander, consecrated this shrine of Mahadeva, praised here as the emperor of temples.

i18n.hi: ईटगी की चट्टान पर लेखकों ने गर्व से उकेरा: विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ के शासन में सेनापति महादेव ने महादेव का यह मंदिर प्रतिष्ठित किया, जिसे यहाँ मंदिरों के सम्राट की उपाधि दी गई है।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over Deccan landscape with distant city
panels.action: High view over dry fields and rocky outcrops leading to the fortified city of Kalyani, banners fluttering above palace roofs as troops drill in the courtyards and brahmins move through bustling streets.

dialogue.text: Under the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani, c. 1112 CE, power moved through forts, courts and armies. Yet their rule also marched in stone, in a flowering of temples across the Deccan.

i18n.hi: कल्याणी के पश्चिमी चालुक्यों के तहत, लगभग १११२ ई., ताकत किलों, दरबारों और सेनाओं से चलती थी। फिर भी उनका राज पत्थरों में भी चलता रहा—दक्कनभर में खिलते मंदिरों की कतारों में।

panels.shot: medium shot in royal durbar hall
panels.action: Mahadeva the Commander stands in a royal audience hall before an unseen king’s throne, flanked by officials; he wears a general’s ornaments and holds a helmet at his side, his posture disciplined and loyal.

dialogue.text: Mahadeva appears in this record not as priest or architect, but as a commander in royal service, moving between campaigns and court, where loyalty was measured in land grants and remembered in stone.

i18n.hi: इस अभिलेख में महादेव न पुरोहित है, न वास्तुकार, बल्कि राजसेवा में सेनापति है—मुहिमों और दरबार के बीच चलता, जहाँ वफादारी ज़मीन के इनाम में तौली जाती और पत्थर में दर्ज होती।

panels.shot: wide shot of rural Itagi site, empty ground
panels.action: Mahadeva stands upon a bare rock-strewn rise at Itagi, gesturing toward the open sky as local masons and laborers look on; chalk lines mark the future plan on the ground.

dialogue.text: At Itagi, in today’s Koppal district, he chose a rise above the fields. Here would stand his offering to Mahadeva—combining courtly ambition, religious merit and the finest craft of his age.

i18n.hi: आज के कोप्पल ज़िले के ईटगी में उसने खेतों से ऊपर उठती जगह चुनी—यहीं खड़ा होगा उसका महादेव को अर्पण: दरबारी महत्वाकांक्षा, धार्मिक पुण्य और अपने दौर की बेहतरीन कारीगरी का संगम।

panels.action: Inside a half-built stone hall, early pillars rise; Mahadeva watches artisans shape blocks while overseers confer beside marked plans, dust floating in shafts of light from the open roof.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars place Itagi’s temple in the maturing Western Chalukya style, a Vesara blend between Deccan Nagara towers and Dravida forms, not an isolated miracle but a high point in a long evolution.

i18n.hi: विद्वान ईटगी के मंदिर को पकते पश्चिमी चालुक्य शैली में रखते हैं—वेसरा रूप, जहाँ दक्कनी नागर शिखर और द्रविड रूप मिलते हैं; कोई अकेला चमत्कार नहीं, बल्कि लंबी यात्रा की चोटी।

panels.shot: tight focus on lathe-turned pillar being carved
panels.action: Artisans crouch around a cylindrical stone shaft mounted for turning; the emerging lathe-turned pillar gleams with smooth rings and sharp flutes as Mahadeva leans in, studying its refinement.

dialogue.text: The inscription omits the architect’s name. The art lies in anonymous hands: carvers perfecting lathe-turned pillars, polishing stone into smooth drums and crisp moldings that catch light like metal.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख वास्तुकार का नाम नहीं बताता। कला अनाम हाथों में है—कतराश जिन्होंने मशीनी-सी स्तंभ तराशे, पत्थर को चिकने ड्रमों और पैने किनारों में घिसा जो धातु की तरह रोशनी पकड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide interior shot showing layout progression
panels.action: A cutaway-like view shows the temple’s axial plan: dark sanctum, a short vestibule, a closed hall, and an open mantapa, pillars marching outward in ordered ranks as Mahadeva walks along the axis.

dialogue.text: Itagi’s planning is clear and disciplined: a garbhagriha for Mahadeva, a vestibule, a closed hall, then an open pillared mantapa, with subsidiary shrines anchored around, forming a stone city of worship.

i18n.hi: ईटगी की योजना साफ और अनुशासित है: महादेव का गर्भगृह, फिर अंतरााल, बंद मंडप, आगे खुला स्तंभित मंडप; चारों ओर छोटे मंदिर जमे हुए, जैसे पत्थर की नगरी में पूजा का नगर।

panels.shot: slow push-in through forest of pillars
panels.action: From floor level, the camera looks down the long open hall as sixty-four pillars rise in measured rows; Mahadeva walks between them, his figure small against the patterned stone forest.

dialogue.text: The hall at Itagi bristles with sixty-four pillars, each turned, carved and set so that stone becomes rhythm—an ordered forest through which processions will move and chants will echo for centuries.

i18n.hi: ईटगी का मंडप चौसठ स्तंभों से खिंचा है—हर एक घिसा, तराशा, जड़ा हुआ—पत्थर को लय बना देता है; सजा हुआ वन, जिसमें से जुलूस गुजरेंगे और मंत्रों की गूँज सदियों तक घूमेगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of deity installation in shrine
panels.action: In the dim sanctum, priests lower a linga onto a stone pedestal while lamps burn; Mahadeva stands at the threshold, hands joined, his armor softened by the flickering light.

dialogue.text: When the linga was set in the shrine and ritual smoke curled through the vestibule, Mahadeva’s role as commander met his role as patron. He had given his king devotion, and now gave his god a house.

i18n.hi: जब लिंग गर्भगृह में स्थापित हुआ और धुएँ की लहरें अंतरााल में उठीं, तब सेनापति महादेव की भूमिका उसके संरक्षक रूप से मिल गई। उसने राजा को भक्ति दी थी, अब अपने देव को घर दे रहा था।

panels.shot: low-angle of temple shikhara against sky
panels.action: The stepped tower above the sanctum rises against a clear sky, articulation sharp yet compact; Mahadeva looks up from the courtyard, dwarfed by the vertical climb of stone.

dialogue.text: The tower above Itagi’s sanctum speaks a Deccan Nagara language in Western Chalukya idiom—compact, layered, finely cut—one note in a wider Vesara chorus that stretched across their realm.

i18n.hi: ईटगी के गर्भगृह के ऊपर का शिखर दक्कनी नागर भाषा बोलता है, पर पश्चिमी चालुक्य लहजे में—संक्षिप्त, परतदार, बारीक तराशा—वेसरा के बड़े गीत में एक स्वर जो उनके राज्यभर में फैला।

panels.shot: close-up on inscription carver at work
panels.action: A stonecutter kneels beside the finished temple wall, carefully chiseling the foundation inscription while Mahadeva dictates to a scribe, his expression steady but intent.

dialogue.speaker: mahadeva_the_commander
dialogue.text: Write it so the future knows whose age and whose hand raised this.

i18n.hi: इसे यूँ लिखो कि आने वाला समय जाने, किसके युग और किसके हाथों ने इसे उठाया।

panels.shot: medium shot of inscription tablet set upright
panels.action: The newly carved inscription slab is stood upright near the entrance; Mahadeva watches as attendants fix it into the ground, the temple looming behind him.

dialogue.text: The inscription names Vikramaditya VI’s reign, Mahadeva’s command, the dedication to Mahadeva, and dares to hail this temple as an emperor—a stone sovereign among shrines.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ का शासन, महादेव की सेनानायकी, महादेव को समर्पण सब दर्ज करता है—और साहस से इस मंदिर को सम्राट कहता है, छोटों के बीच पत्थर का सम्राट।

panels.shot: wide festive scene of consecration ceremony
panels.action: Crowds fill the mantapa and courtyard: brahmins chant, dancers perform, villagers watch, while Mahadeva offers flowers to the deity; the sixty-four pillars frame the ceremony like silent witnesses.

dialogue.text: On consecration day, sound and color flooded the stone. Yet the lasting act was quieter: the alignment of halls, the exact carving of pillars, the measured placing of shrines, all rooted to royal patronage.

i18n.hi: प्रतिष्ठा के दिन पत्थर पर स्वर और रंगों की बाढ़ आई। पर टिकने वाला काम शांत था—मंडपों का संतुलन, स्तंभों की सटीक नक्काशी, मंदिरों की नपी-तुली जड़, सब राजाश्रय से बंधे हुए।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide, temple enduring through changing skies
panels.action: The temple stands in stillness as the light shifts from dawn to dusk, clouds streaming overhead; Mahadeva’s figure fades like a ghost at the edge of the frame, leaving only stone.

dialogue.text: Kings, commanders and priests would pass. The temple’s architecture, formed by a mature Western Chalukya craft, remained, carrying memory of Vikramaditya’s age and Mahadeva’s patronage into later centuries.

i18n.hi: राजा, सेनापति और पुरोहित सब चले गए। पर परिपक्व पश्चिमी चालुक्य कला से बनी यह रचना टिक गई, विक्रमादित्य के युग और महादेव की संरक्षकता की स्मृति लेकर आगे की सदियों में जाती रही।

panels.shot: archaeological survey style wide with modern scholar observing
panels.action: In a more recent time, a scholar stands with notebook in the open hall, studying the pillars and plan; Mahadeva’s stone image on a wall panel looks on, worn but recognizable.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, surveyors and historians—Cousens, Dhaky, Meister, Hardy—would walk these same halls, reading its plan and carvings as documents of Vesara development in the Western Chalukya heartland.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद सर्वेक्षक और इतिहासकार—कूज़न्स, धाकी, माइसटर, हार्डी—यही मंडप नापते चलेंगे, इसकी योजना और नक्काशी को वेसरा विकास की दस्तावेज़ मानकर पश्चिमी चालुक्य केंद्र में पढ़ेंगे।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot, single pillar in foreground
panels.action: A single lathe-turned pillar fills the frame, polished rings catching soft light; beyond it, Mahadeva’s faint, imagined silhouette stands near the sanctum, hands joined, face unreadable.

dialogue.text: The record shows no battles here, only stone: a commander’s loyalty translated into architecture, a temple crowned as emperor among its peers, and craft made to hold power’s memory after its voice fell silent.

i18n.hi: अभिलेख यहाँ कोई युद्ध नहीं दिखाता, सिर्फ पत्थर: सेनापति की वफादारी जो वास्तु बन गई, मंदिर जो अपने साथियों में सम्राट का ताज पहनता है, और कारीगरी जो सत्ता की याद को संभाले रखती है, जब उसकी आवाज़ ख़ामोश हो चुकी होती है।

title_i18n.en: Itagi Becomes the Emperor of Temples

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Chalukya general raised a stone ‘emperor’ to outlast kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक चालुक्य सेनापति ने पत्थर का ‘सम्राट’ बनाया जो राजाओं से भी लंबा चले
